content:
Quick comments first.

Formatting / presentation
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly following the example there.

Variable names
* Please use the same variable names in the Input section, the Constraints section and the stub generator.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement.

I'll perform a more detailed review later.

Thanks.

Goal
* Please briefly explain how packet generation, buffer size and capacity relate to packet loss condition.

* Players shouldn't be assumed to know either Poisson distributions or Chernoff bounds. Please include the minimum explanation of the concepts required to solve the puzzle, or at least provide a relevant link.

Input
* Please change "Line 1: n lambda_u C L" to "<<Line 1>>: Four space-separated numbers".

* Please specify the type of each variable (integer or float).

Output
* Please format "Line 1" in <<bold>>.

Variable formatting
* Please note that variables don't need to be formatted in <<bold>>. However, it's fine to leave the formatting unchanged.

Tags
* Please replace the current tags with two existing and more generic ones instead: Probability, Binary search.

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario with similar inputs and outputs. Please

  • Split Test 1 and Validator 1 into two pairs.

  • Add a new validator to go with Test 1, e.g. 4 0.26 9 0.14.

  • Add a new test to go with Validator 1, e.g. 19 1.13 26 0.36.

  • Use new inputs for Test 3 to match Validator 3, e.g. 7 0.24 2 0.77.

* Please add two new pairs of cases to cover the currently missing scenario where chernoff_poisson(lam, C + mid) is always greater than L during binary search:

  • 94 8.83 867 0.31

  • 254 2.85 738 0.54

  • 354 1.6 333 0.65

  • 307 1.54 247 0.4

Thanks.
